plan_rq.help: Start from a literature review: what causes what? An experiment is "a test designed to objectively observe phenomena which are made to occur in a strictly controlled situation where one or more variables are varied, and the others are held constant." (Meeting 1)
plan_rq.placeholder: e.g. Does a larger choice set (30 vs 6 candies) change decision difficulty and satisfaction?

plan_hyp.help: H₀: no difference / no effect. H₁: an effect exists. A one-sided test needs the direction fixed before seeing the data; p is halved only when the data go the predicted way.

options.label: Two-sided (≠)
options.consequence: Choose this if any difference counts, in either direction.

options.label: One-sided: first group / condition higher (>)
options.consequence: Choose this only if theory predicts the direction in advance.

options.label: One-sided: first group / condition lower (<)
options.consequence: Choose this only if theory predicts the direction in advance.

plan_vars.help: IV: manipulated on purpose (its levels are the conditions). DV: the measured outcome. Control variables: held constant. Data type (NOIR): Nominal, Ordinal, Interval, Ratio. t-tests, ANOVA and linear regression need an interval/ratio DV. Operational definitions make the study replicable.

plan_manip.text: Can you manipulate the IV and randomly assign units to conditions?
plan_manip.help: A true experiment gives the strongest basis for a causal claim (cause first, co-variation, no confound). Pre-existing groups (gender, age) or a surveyed continuous IV make it a quasi-experiment.

options.label: Yes: true experiment
options.consequence: Strongest causal claim.

options.label: No: quasi-experiment
options.consequence: Pre-existing groups or surveyed IV; the causal claim is weaker.

plan_controls.text: Which experimental controls will you build in?
plan_controls.help: Randomize assignment and run order. Counterbalance order to control carryover: full = all n! orders; Latin square = n orders, each condition once per row and column. Block nuisance factors (subject, batch, operator) → randomized complete block design.

lane.text: What is the research goal, and what type are the DV and IV(s)?
lane.help: Match the goal and the variable types to a lane, then follow that lane's decisions.

options.label: A · Compare conditions
options.consequence: Numeric DV; categorical IV(s) with a few set levels → t-tests and ANOVA.

options.label: B · Model a relationship
options.consequence: Numeric DV; continuous IV(s), predict the DV → linear regression.

options.label: C · Categorical outcome
options.consequence: DV is a category (yes/no) or counts in a table → logistic regression / χ².

options.label: D · Engineering optimization
options.consequence: Many controllable factors: screen → optimize → make robust.

A_niv.help: Each IV is a factor; its levels are the conditions.

options.label: One IV
options.consequence: t-test or one-way ANOVA.

options.label: Two or more IVs (factorial)
options.consequence: Factorial, repeated measures or mixed ANOVA.

A_levels.text: How many levels does the IV have?
A_levels.help: Why not many t-tests? Each test adds Type I risk (10 tests ≈ 40% false-alarm chance). Use one ANOVA, then corrected post hoc tests. (Meeting 6)

options.label: 2 levels
options.consequence: A t-test.

options.label: 3 or more levels
options.consequence: A one-way ANOVA.

A_within2.text: Does every participant do both levels?
A_within2.help: Within gives fewer people, removes individual differences and has more power, but risks carryover (practice, fatigue). Counterbalancing controls carryover. If learning effects are large and hard to counterbalance, use between.

options.label: No: between-subject
options.consequence: Each person sees one level.

options.label: Yes: within-subject
options.consequence: Each person does both levels.

A_within3.text: Does every participant do every level?
A_within3.help: Within gives fewer people, removes individual differences and has more power, but risks carryover (practice, fatigue). Block design = within-subject in engineering terms (subject = block).

options.label: No: between-subject
options.consequence: Each person sees one level.

options.label: Yes: within-subject (or blocks)
options.consequence: Each person does every level.

A_nfactors.help: Four-way and higher interactions are very hard to explain. Up to a three-way interaction is usually the most that can be explained.
A_nfactors.warn: Four-way and higher interactions are very hard to explain.

A_mix.text: Is each IV within or between?
A_mix.help: Mixed design: at least one within IV and one between IV (e.g. gender between × task within). Sphericity applies to the within factors, homogeneity of variance to the between factors.

options.label: All between
options.consequence: Factorial (n-way) between-subjects ANOVA.

options.label: All within
options.consequence: Two-way (n-way) repeated-measures ANOVA.

options.label: Some of each (mixed)
options.consequence: Mixed (split-plot) ANOVA.

B_npred.help: ANOVA or regression? ANOVA: a few set levels, no shape assumed, any design. Regression: continuous IV, assumes a function, can predict new values.

options.label: One predictor
options.consequence: Simple linear regression.

options.label: Two or more predictors
options.consequence: Multiple linear regression.

B_theory.text: Is the order of the predictors theory-driven or data-driven?
B_theory.help: Forward entry: the predictor with the highest simple correlation enters first, then the one with the largest semi-partial correlation.

options.label: Theory-driven
options.consequence: Hierarchical / Enter in blocks; report ΔR² and F change.

options.label: Data-driven
options.consequence: Forward, backward or stepwise; watch for overfitting.

C_type.text: What does the categorical data look like?
C_type.help: The odds ratio multiplies the odds, not the probability. k levels → k − 1 dummies.

options.label: Binary DV (2 outcomes)
options.consequence: Binary logistic regression.

options.label: Categorical IV × categorical DV (counts)
options.consequence: χ² test of independence (Fisher's exact when expected counts < 5).

options.label: DV with 3+ categories
options.consequence: Multinomial logistic regression: not covered in SYDE 640.

D_goal.text: Where are you in the engineering process?
D_goal.help: 2ᵏ designs are for screening (early engineering, linear effects), not for finding causal mechanisms.

options.label: Many candidate factors: which few matter?
options.consequence: Factor screening with a 2ᵏ or 2ᵏ⁻ᵖ design.

options.label: Active factors known: find the best settings
options.consequence: Response surface methodology (curvature, steepest ascent, CCD).

options.label: Performance varies with uncontrollable noise
options.consequence: Robust parameter design (Taguchi / response model).

D_budget.text: Is there budget for all 2ᵏ runs?
D_budget.help: One replicate = 2ᵏ runs, in random order. Fractional designs: judge by effect size; they work best when within-condition variation is small.

options.label: Yes, with 2+ replicates
options.consequence: Full-model ANOVA: F test for every effect.

options.label: Yes, but only 1 replicate
options.consequence: Effects, normal plot, then a reduced model.

options.label: No: too many runs
options.consequence: Fractional factorial 2ᵏ⁻ᵖ.

ttest_ind.name: Independent-samples t-test
ttest_ind.fallbacks: Unequal variances → Welch's t-test. Non-normal → Mann-Whitney U.

anova_oneway.name: One-way ANOVA
anova_oneway.fallbacks: Unequal variances → Welch ANOVA + Games-Howell. Non-normal → Kruskal-Wallis + Dunn.

anova_rm1.name: One-way repeated-measures ANOVA
anova_rm1.fallbacks: Mauchly p < .05 → GG if ε < 0.60, else HF. Non-normal → Friedman + Conover.

anova_factorial.name: Factorial (n-way) ANOVA
anova_factorial.fallbacks: No nonparametric version: transform, split + Bonferroni, or caveat.

anova_rm.name: Two-way (n-way) repeated-measures ANOVA
anova_rm.fallbacks: GG/HF per within effect. Non-normal → Friedman one factor at a time, or transform.

anova_mixed.name: Mixed ANOVA (split-plot)
anova_mixed.fallbacks: Within part → GG/HF. Between part → no Welch: transform, split + Bonferroni, or caveat.

regression_simple.name: Simple linear regression
regression_simple.fallbacks: Transform the DV, add polynomial terms, or a GLM.

regression_hier.name: Multiple linear regression (hierarchical)
regression_hier.design: Correlational design, 2+ predictors entered in theory-driven blocks

regression_step.name: Multiple linear regression (forward / backward / stepwise)
regression_step.fallbacks: Watch for overfitting; VIF ≥ 10 → drop or combine predictors.

logistic.name: Binary logistic regression
logistic.design: Binary outcome, numeric and/or categorical predictors

not_covered.name: Multinomial / ordinal logistic regression
not_covered.note: Named in Meeting 14 but not covered in SYDE 640. Consider collapsing to two categories (binary logistic) or a χ² test on the counts.

doe_2k_single.name: Single-replicate 2ᵏ factorial
doe_2k_single.fallbacks: Normal/half-normal plot + Lenth's margin → reduced model; dropped factor → 2ᵏ⁻¹ with replicates.

doe_rsm.name: Response surface methodology
doe_rsm.design: Centre points → steepest ascent → CCD / Box-Behnken

doe_robust.name: Robust parameter design
doe_robust.design: Crossed array (Taguchi) or combined array (response model)
